sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 27

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 27:1
items.html: When the light longs for equivalence of form, to be refined like the Emanator, and is therefore found wanting to depart from its clothing in the vessels, this departure is called “longing for its source.” And this matter is drawn through the striking of inner light and surrounding light one against the other. And you must understand that the intention is not upon the upper light in its self, but upon the ten Sefirot of direct light, which are already in the discernment of a shared relation between the light and its garment — for it is on this account that they are called Sefirot. Indeed, of the self of the upper light we have no utterance or word at all, for there is no attainment of light without a garment or a vessel. (Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 10)
